M2_export_copy_1M.note: Synthesized from 3 independent full runs of export_envelope.mjs (2026-07-27, same session/hardware) — no single run captured every measurement cleanly (the dialog-driven export path is itself intermittently unreliable, which is part of the finding), so this section combines the best/most complete evidence across all 3 with provenance in each entry's notes, rather than reporting only the last run verbatim.

results.notes: click-to-dataset-row-appearing, same path as F1; mean of 3 runs (11641, 11492, 11727 ms)

UNMEASURED: reproducible across all 3 runs — clicking "Run" in the Export figure dialog (fmt=svg) never sends the /api/export/figure request within a 240s window (no fetch, no status change, no toast, no console error). See svg_export_raw_fetch_bypass_ui_ms: the SAME spec posted directly via fetch() (bypassing the dialog/buildFigureSpec orchestration) succeeds in ~16.7s, so this is specific to the UI's dialog-driven path, not the backend endpoint.

click "Run" -> real /api/export/figure POST -> blob captured; mean of 2 SUCCESSFUL runs (16900 ms/165994 bytes, 15343 ms/165994 bytes; both valid PNG headHex=89504e470d0a1a0a). RELIABILITY: succeeded 2 of 3 attempts across runs — the 3rd run's PNG dialog attempt also hung with zero network activity, same failure mode as the SVG case. The dialog-driven export path is intermittently unreliable at this scale, independent of format.
identical across both successful runs

Across 3 independent full-session runs of the "Export figure…" Command Palette dialog on the 1M-row/7-series plot: PNG succeeded 2 of 3 times (16900ms, 15343ms), SVG failed 3 of 3 times (240s timeout, zero network activity each time). "Copy figure" (same render pipeline, reached via right-click instead of the dialog) succeeded 3 of 3 times at ~15s — isolating the unreliability to the ParamDialog-driven flow (askParams -> runExportFigureCommand), not buildFigureSpec/exportFigure/the backend renderer.

direct POST /api/export/figure from page.evaluate (bypasses the "Export figure…" dialog + buildFigureSpec orchestration entirely, replicated the same FigureSpec by hand) — status=200 size=1675056 bytes (SVG, headHex confirms XML). Confirms the BACKEND can render an SVG of this dataset in bounded time (~16.7s, comparable to the PNG dialog's own ~15-17s); the UI-driven svg_export_click_to_file_ms failure above is specific to the frontend orchestration path, not the endpoint.

ClipboardItem.supports('image/svg+xml') — the same gate lib/clipboard.ts's clipboardSvgSupported() uses to decide whether the plot's right-click menu offers "Copy figure (vector)". True in all 3 runs when checked via page.evaluate() directly.

right-click -> "Copy figure" -> real /api/export/figure render (png, 300 DPI, default style) -> navigator.clipboard.write() resolved (context.grantPermissions(['clipboard-read','clipboard-write']) granted at BASE_URL). Succeeded in ALL 3 runs (14921, 15031, 14957 ms; mean 14970 ms) — the most reliable of the export/copy paths measured, since it never goes through the ParamDialog.

UNMEASURED: reproducible in all 3 runs — despite ClipboardItem.supports('image/svg+xml') returning true when probed directly, the live right-click menu never renders a "Copy figure (vector)" entry (confirmed via a dedicated isolated probe on a FRESH page, first action, small dataset: menu shows Line style/Width/Marker/.../Copy figure/Copy image (screen)/Copy data (TSV)/Save as PNG — no vector entry). The app's own gate (usePlotStageActions.ts's clipboardSvgSupported() check, evaluated at component-render time) is disagreeing with an equivalent check run later via page.evaluate() in the same page — plausibly a headless-Chromium focus/user-activation timing difference in ClipboardItem.supports() rather than an app defect, but not chased further (measurement-only task). There is nothing to click, so the gesture cannot be timed.
